claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops a diagnostic only when its location is in source but in another syntax tree. A metadata member has no declaring syntax, so the changed MemberNeedsKey site now builds its diagnostic with a null location (Location.None). IsInSource is false for that location, so the filter lets it through. Concrete input: the referenced assembly defines `[MessagePackObject] public struct Item<T> { public int Value; }` (built without the analyzer, or with MsgPack004 suppressed), and the app has a member of type `Item<int>`. On head the analyzer reports MsgPack004, an Error per L2, with no location in the consuming compilation, so a build that only crashed with warnings on base now fails. This contradicts L8 (metadata types are deliberately not diagnosed by the consumer) and the helper's own remark that such problems are dropped. The same leak applies with AllowPrivate=true, where metadata backing fields such as `<Key>k__BackingField` are private fields without [Key].

claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation only drops diagnostics whose location is in source of another compilation. Diagnostics with no location (Location.None, from FirstOrDefault() null) pass the filter (IsInSource is false). Diagnostics for metadata-only closed generic structs (MsgPack004 MemberNeedsKey, MsgPack003 etc.) are therefore still reported with no location in users' builds, so a defining assembly's non-annotated members could surface as new location-less errors/warnings in the consuming project. MsgPack004 is an Error (L2), so a previously silent build (generator crashed) may now fail. The filter condition is inverted relative to its doc comment.
